rules_applied: Standardized missing string placeholders ('?', 'NA', 'N/A', 'null') to NaN.
Numeric columns with skewness > 1.0 or < -1.0 use median imputation.
Numeric columns with skewness between -1.0 and 1.0 use mean imputation.
Categorical/String columns use mode imputation with 'Unknown' fallback.

engineered_features.rationale: Total infrastructure availability is often a stronger predictor of EV-related behavior than home or work alone.
Financial capacity relative to existing vehicle overhead.

feature_selection_strategy: Exclude high-cardinality ID or text name columns
Rank features using cross-validated permutation importance and mutual information
Remove collinear features exceeding correlation threshold > 0.85
validation_strategy: Evaluate Balanced Accuracy, Macro F1, Precision-Recall AUC, and Confusion Matrix
overfitting_risk_mitigation: Limit tree depth and enforce minimum samples per leaf
Perform hyperparameter tuning strictly within cross-validation folds
predictive_modeling_blueprint.executive_summary: Target: 'Current_Car_Type' (Multiclass Classification). Model recommendations and validation strategy tailored for 10000 rows x 12 columns.

bivariate_data.rationale: Categorical breakdown of Gender by City_Type

union_pairs.rationale: This pair explores life-stage patterns in driving behavior, helping to determine which age demographics have commute profiles most compatible with current EV ranges.
This pair helps identify if higher-income individuals have better access to charging infrastructure, which is a key driver for EV adoption and overcoming range anxiety.
This interaction highlights the disparity in residential charging availability between Urban, Suburban, and Rural areas, which dictates the feasibility of EV ownership.

This helps segment the market to see if financial capacity per vehicle influences the choice of more expensive or specialized vehicle types like SUVs and Trucks. (Also identified statistically by algorithms)
Analyzing these together reveals whether individuals with longer commutes—who are more susceptible to range anxiety—have the necessary charging infrastructure to support an EV.
